source.title: Sveci su pobjednici – Svetkovina Svih svetih i Dušni dan [Škola Riječi #188]

summary.title_hr: Sveci su pobjednici – Svetkovina Svih svetih i Dušni dan [Škola Riječi #188]
summary.abstract_hr: U ovoj epizodi Škole Riječi predavač tumači prvo čitanje sa svetkovine Svih svetih, odlomak iz 7. poglavlja knjige Otkrivenja o viđenju vidioca Ivana na nebu. Obrazlaže simboliku 144 000 opečaćenih, neizbrojivog mnoštva u bijelim haljinama s palmama, Jaganjca, starješina i četiriju bića. Ističe da je knjiga Otkrivenja, unatoč zastrašujućim prizorima, duboko optimistična jer unaprijed naviješta konačnu pobjedu dobra nad zlom te poziva čovjeka da se svrsta na stranu pobjednika. Na kraju povezuje svetkovinu Svih svetih sa spomenom svih vjernih mrtvih 2. studenoga i s običajem posjećivanja grobova pokojnika.
key_points: Broj od 144 000 opečaćenih je simboličan i izveden je iz broja 12. Taj broj spaja stari i novi Božji narod, odnosno 12 plemena Izraelovih i 12 Jaganjčevih apostola, a označava veliko mnoštvo spašenih.

Uz opečaćene iz Izraela spašeno je i neizbrojivo mnoštvo iz svakoga naroda, plemena, puka i jezika. Predavač zato knjigu Otkrivenja smatra optimističnom porukom da je većina ljudi na svijetu dobra i da želi mir.
Jednaka čast koja se iskazuje onome koji sjedi na prijestolju i Jaganjcu slikovito izražava vjeru da su Otac i Sin iste božanske naravi.
Bijele haljine oprane u krvi Jaganjčevoj paradoksalna su slika očišćenja od grijeha. Palme se ovdje ne odnose samo na mučenike, nego na sve krštene koji su izdržali životne borbe.

Znak kojim su opečaćene sluge Božje preuzet je iz knjige proroka Ezekiela. Riječ je o znaku Tau, koji je u starohebrejskom pismu imao oblik križa pa su ga kršćani prepoznavali kao simbol Kristova križa.
Četiri bića s licem čovjeka, vola, lava i orla danas se koriste kao simboli evanđelista. U biblijskom kontekstu ona predstavljaju sva živa stvorenja koja slave Boga.

Temeljna poruka knjige Otkrivenja jest da posljednja riječ pripada dobru, a ne zlu. Na svetkovinu Svih svetih slave se svi, kanonizirani i nekanonizirani, koji su se u životu svrstali na stranu pobjednika.
key_topics_en: the sign tau and the cross
all souls' day and commemoration of the deceased
key_points_en: The number of 144,000 sealed is symbolic and is derived from the number 12. That number unites the old and the new people of God, namely the 12 tribes of Israel and the 12 apostles of the Lamb, and signifies a great multitude of the saved.

Along with the sealed from Israel, an innumerable multitude from every nation, tribe, people, and language is also saved. The lecturer therefore considers the Book of Revelation an optimistic message that the majority of people in the world are good and desire peace.
The equal honor rendered to the one sitting on the throne and to the Lamb vividly expresses the faith that the Father and the Son are of the same divine nature.

The white robes washed in the blood of the Lamb are a paradoxical image of cleansing from sin. The palm branches here refer not only to martyrs, but to all the baptized who have endured life's struggles.

The mark with which the servants of God are sealed is taken from the book of the prophet Ezekiel. It is the sign Tau, which in ancient Hebrew script had the shape of a cross, so Christians recognized it as a symbol of Christ's cross.

The four living creatures with the face of a human, an ox, a lion, and an eagle are used today as symbols of the evangelists. In the biblical context, they represent all living creatures praising God.

The fundamental message of the Book of Revelation is that the final word belongs to good, not evil. On the Solemnity of All Saints, all are celebrated, canonized and uncanonized, who in life aligned themselves on the side of the victors.
summary.title_en: Saints Are Victors – Solemnity of All Saints and All Souls' Day [School of the Word #188]
summary.abstract_en: In this episode of the School of the Word, the lecturer interprets the first reading from the Solemnity of All Saints, a passage from chapter 7 of the Book of Revelation about the vision of the seer John in heaven. He explains the symbolism of the 144,000 sealed, the innumerable multitude in white robes with palm branches, the Lamb, the elders, and the four living creatures. He emphasizes that the Book of Revelation, despite its terrifying scenes, is deeply optimistic because it proclaims in advance the final victory of good over evil and calls man to align himself on the side of the victors. In the end, he connects the Solemnity of All Saints with the commemoration of all the faithful departed on November 2 and with the custom of visiting the graves of the deceased.
